symptom: Two consecutive activities with custom error handlers and no @position drew their handler rows on top of each other: the first handler's end event and the second handler's first activity both at 680;330 ($First 360;200, $Body 520;200, $Second 680;200). layout flows --dry-run said 'already laid out' (same builder), MPR008 said nothing (end events not compared), mx check 0 errors. A @position on a later statement also moved every unplaced statement before it onto that statement.
cause: addErrorHandlerFlow built the row 130px under the activity, running right, but never reserved the lower lane, while clearLowerLane already made the next activity with a handler wait for a reserved lane (the #1154 guard design); measureStatements likewise reserved only for guards and left handler rows out of the extent that fitContainerSize counts, so a loop with a long trailing row was built 110px wider than measured. Case 2: buildFlowGraph's start pre-scan took the first statement WITH an @position instead of the first statement.
insight: The lane model already stated the rule ('an activity with an error handler waits for the lane'); one of the lane's two occupants never registered itself. Look for the occupant that does not reserve before inventing a mechanism. Reserve from the measurer, in builder and measurer alike: the builder-only half (control) left 12 shapes with a merge landing on an activity. Studio Pro reference: all 8 multi-object handlers in PedApp and ako/TestApp are COLUMNS straight under the activity (80-130px per step), none is a row and none has a consecutive pair; a column layout would make the collision impossible but moves every flow with a 2+ statement handler and needs a vertical layout for compound handler bodies, so the lane was kept (2 of 182 example flows move). Two older measurer gaps surfaced by the new invariant test and were left alone: an IF is measured 45px short (the split's centre is counted as its left edge in guardBranchInset and measureIfStatement), and a `join` is measured as an activity plus an end event although it draws nothing, so a handler row ending in joins reserves about twice its drawn width. Check overlaps with the whole node set: MPR008 skipped events, which hid exactly this overlap; on 292 Studio Pro flows the wider set adds 0 findings.
